endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: This element also considers whether the device defers appropriately when information is insufficient, without over-deferring when adequate information is available.

endorsements.title: Large language models could change the future of behavioral healthcare: a proposal for responsible development and evaluation
endorsements.quote: Clinical LLMs can abide by this ethical standard by drawing on integrated assessment (discussed above) to assess the appropriateness of the given intervention and detect cases that need more specialized or intensive intervention.

endorsements.title: Expert Consensus Best Practices for the Safe, Ethical, and Effective Design and Implementation of Artificially Intelligent Conversational Agent (i.e., Chatbot/Virtual Human) Systems in Health Care Applications
endorsements.quote: In addition, the AICA should be designed to defer to professionals when needed to prevent users from developing a dependency on the AICA for diagnosis and treatment of serious health conditions.

endorsements.title: Augmenting research consent: should large language models (LLMs) be used for informed consent to clinical research?
endorsements.quote: It would therefore be essential that LLMs are programmed to recognise the limits of their capabilities, and to refer users to human researchers when questions exceed the AI’s scope of knowledge or when a human-based approach is required.

endorsements.title: A nursing perspective on human-AI collaboration in personalized breast cancer care pathways
endorsements.quote: Furthermore, mandatory escalation protocols are required in three specific scenarios: when the AI system indicates low confidence in its output, when it operates outside its validated scope, or when a disagreement between the clinician and the algorithm involves potentially high-risk outcomes ( 63 – 65 ).

endorsements.title: AI Agents Are Coming: 5-Stage Taxonomy of Language-Based AI Systems for Psychiatry, Psychotherapy, and Counseling
endorsements.quote: Systems assess and communicate ambiguity to call for human supervision when needed

evidence.title: Blueprint for Safety: Implementing a Clinically Governed AI Digital Assistant for Patient Guidance
evidence.venue: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
evidence.outcome: Standard-risk queries routed to human support
evidence.effect: Standard-risk queries routed to human support decreased by 65%. The abstract does not quantify missed high-risk deferrals.
evidence.quote: Using a randomized rollout to half of the patient population, the authors found that the risk-stratified assistant maintained a high level of clinical safety (96% accurate guidance, 0% critical safety events, and no AI-generated diagnoses) while reducing standard-risk queries routed to human support by 65%, shortening average human response times from 9.6 to 3.6 minutes, and improving resolution of health inquiries without additional visits.

evidence.title: From Concept to Clinic: Real World Evidence for Autonomous AI Deployment in Primary Care Telemedicine
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic concordance with and without a pre-specified safety confidence threshold
evidence.effect: Top-1 diagnosis matched clinicians in 91.3% overall, rising to 96.3% among cases meeting the pre-specified safety confidence threshold.
evidence.quote: The AI’s top-1 diagnosis matched the clinician’s diagnosis in 91.3% of cases overall, increasing to 96.3% among cases meeting a pre-specified safety confidence threshold, and 97.9% in common, lower-complexity conditions that met the same confidence threshold.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence for Kidney Stone Spectra Analysis: Using Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Quality Assurance in the Clinical Laboratory
evidence.outcome: Concordance among predictions selected for automatic classification versus secondary human review
evidence.effect: Concordance was 98.7% (95% CI, 98.56%-98.9%) for autoPass candidates versus 84.3% (95% CI, 84.0%-84.6%) for cases flagged for manual secondary review.
evidence.quote: When the stone spectra were grouped into those stones selected for autoPass (candidate for automatic classification) and those not selected (flagged for manual secondary review), the concordance rates were 98.7% (95% CI, 98.56%-98.9%) and 84.3% (95% CI, 84.0%-84.6%), respectively.

evidence.title: Standard-of-Care vs. Machine Learning–Recommended Discharge Destinations for Geriatric Surgical Inpatients: Algorithm Development and Internal Validation
evidence.outcome: accuracy after uncertainty-based deferral
evidence.effect: Excluding the 15% highest-uncertainty predictions increased remaining accuracy to 85% (p = 0.006).
evidence.quote: Mimicking a human-in-the-loop strategy, we excluded the 15% of predictions with the highest uncertainty, which increased accuracy for the remaining predictions to 85% (p = 0.006).

evidence.title: Uncertainty-aware extraction of clinical findings from Finnish EHRs using open large language models
evidence.outcome: selective expert review error coverage
evidence.effect: Complete error coverage by reviewing 8.3% hemiplegia, 8.2% headache, and 19.6% seizure patients.
evidence.quote: Entropy-based triage achieved complete error coverage by reviewing <10% of patients for hemiplegia (8.3%) and headache (8.2%), and 19.6% for seizure.

evidence.title: A framework for human-artificial intelligence co-learning for disease activity labeling using electronic health records
evidence.outcome: ambiguity flag agreement
evidence.effect: Ambiguity flag agreed with expert ambiguity designations with 92.1% accuracy.
evidence.quote: Against this reference, the final agent’s accuracy improved from a mean absolute error of 0.406 to 0.291 with co-learning, and its ambiguity flag agreed with expert ambiguity designations with 92.1% accuracy.

evidence.title: Clinical evaluation of artificial intelligence for diagnostics of antibiotic-resistant bacteria
evidence.outcome: error reduction and abstention rate
evidence.effect: Conformal prediction reduced errors while abstaining in 9.6%, 14%, and 22% of instances at 90%, 95%, and 97.5% confidence levels, versus 19% major and 12% very major error rates without it.
evidence.quote: Conformal prediction reduced errors but increased abstentions; at confidence levels of 90%, 95%, and 97.5%, the model abstained in 9.6%, 14%, and 22% of instances.

evidence.title: A hybrid approach to scalable real-world data curation by machine learning and human experts
evidence.outcome: error rates and manual abstraction burden
evidence.effect: Hybrid curation achieved expert-level error rates with only small amounts of manual abstraction.
evidence.quote: Only small amounts of manual abstraction are required for hybrid curation to achieve expert-level error rates.

evidence.title: Collaborative strategies for deploying artificial intelligence to complement physician diagnoses of acute respiratory distress syndrome
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI-first strategy deferring uncertain cases to physicians vs AI alone or physician alone
evidence.effect: AI deferring to physician if uncertain: accuracy 0.869 (0.835-0.903) vs AI alone 0.847 and physician alone 0.808; physician review burden only 20.7%.
evidence.quote: The physician-aided AI strategy, which defers the diagnosis to physicians only if the AI model is uncertain, resulted in improved diagnostic accuracy than both physician- and AI-alone.

evidence.title: Enhancing the reliability and accuracy of AI-enabled diagnosis via complementarity-driven deferral to clinicians
evidence.outcome: False positives, false negatives and clinician workload when AI defers uncertain cases to clinical workflow
evidence.effect: Breast screening: 25% fewer false positives at same false-negative rate versus UK double reading with arbitration, with 66% less clinician workload. TB triage: 5-15% fewer false positives for three of five AI systems.
evidence.quote: For breast cancer screening, compared to double reading with arbitration in a screening program in the UK, CoDoC reduced false positives by 25% at the same false-negative rate, while achieving a 66% reduction in clinician workload.

evidence.title: AI-clinician collaboration via disagreement prediction: A decision pipeline and retrospective analysis of real-world radiologist-AI interactions
evidence.outcome: Burden impact of deferring/second-read requests on predicted disagreement findings
evidence.effect: Even if all clinically significant disagreements receive a second read, burden increases only 6.67% ± 0.07%; restricting to under 5% reduces burden by 4.8% ± 0.1%.
evidence.quote: Even if all cases of disagreement on clinically significant findings receive a second read, burden is only increased by 6.67% ± 0.07%.

evidence.title: A Human-Centered AI Framework for Efficient Labelling of ECGs From Drug Safety Trials
evidence.outcome: ECG labelling effort and QT accuracy
evidence.effect: On 3 drug safety trials, only 10% of data were reviewed per trial while maintaining high QT accuracy.
evidence.quote: We assess its effectiveness on 3 drug safety trials and show that it can significantly reduce effort required for ECG labelling-in our experiments only 10% of the data were reviewed per trial-while maintaining high levels of QT accuracy.

evidence.title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: Selective prediction (abstention/deferral to humans) effect on LLM F1 performance
evidence.effect: Consistency-based deferral raised F1 to 0.85-0.88 (step 1) and 0.62-0.73 (step 2); verbalized confidence gave narrower ranges (0.58-0.69 step 2); gains marginal due to poor calibration.
evidence.quote: Selective prediction marginally improved the LLM’s filtering accuracy by enabling it to defer uncertain cases to human reviewers.

evidence.title: Confidence-linked and uncertainty-based staged framework for phenotype validation using large language models
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Deferral of uncertain cases to human review while maintaining accuracy and reducing review burden
evidence.effect: Manual review burden reduced by 75%; overall F1 rose from 0.840 (stage 1) to 0.878 (stage 2) to 0.955 (stage 3) with 285 of 1072 cases referred for manual review.
evidence.quote: The CLUES framework reduced manual review burden by 75% while maintaining high accuracy.

evidence.title: Deep learning based semi-automated model can predict lineage in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and workload reduction with confidence-based deferral to IHC and manual review
evidence.effect: In the prospective cohort, confidence-based deferral achieved 68.9% workload reduction and 95.9% overall accuracy; comparison with fully manual IHC-based evaluation: p = 0.610.
evidence.quote: In prospective validation, this approach achieved a 68.9% reduction in diagnostic workload while maintaining 95.9% overall accuracy.

evidence.title: Benchmarking robustness of automated CT pancreas segmentation: achieving human-level reliability through human-in-the-loop optimization
evidence.outcome: Uncertainty-based triage identifying cases to defer to humans for revision
evidence.effect: Acquisition function (entropy + sphericity) inversely correlated with DSC/NSD; revising 6% of cases reduced error rate (1 – FT) to ~1%.
evidence.quote: Instead, an active learning approach proved effective in this case, reducing the error rate (1 – FT) to ∼1% with manual revision of only 6% of cases, leading to a 23-fold workload reduction.
evidence.sample_unit: test CT scans (each with 4 independent human segmentations)

evidence.title: Next-generation multicenter studies: using artificial intelligence to automatically process unstructured health records of patients with lung cancer across multiple institutions
evidence.venue: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
evidence.outcome: data extraction error rate
evidence.effect: error rate decreased from 7.0% to 4.4% with targeted human review of 30% low-confidence outputs
evidence.quote: A hybrid approach with targeted human review of 30% of low-confidence AI outputs further decreased error rates to 4.4%.

evidence.title: Human-AI collaboration enhances the performance of large language models in risk of bias assessment
evidence.outcome: Deferral to humans triggered by low confidence or model disagreement; accuracy and intervention rate
evidence.effect: Predictions with confidence >0.8 were 16.78% to 29.23% more accurate than those ≤0.8; M3 reduced intervention (e.g., DB -40%) with accuracy roughly maintained in structured tasks.
evidence.quote: Across the six domains (DB, SB-IRSG, PB, RB, OB, AB), model predictions with confidence scores above 0.8 consistently showed substantially higher accuracy than those with scores ≤ 0.8, with performance gaps ranging from 16.78% to 29.23% (Appendix 5).
evidence.sample_unit: domain-level RCT risk-of-bias assessments (300 per domain across 7 domains; 60 per domain in human-AI collaboration round)

evidence.title: Colon-Pilot: A Generative AI Tool for Automated Colonoscopy Surveillance Recommendations and 2024 ACG/ASGE Quality Benchmarking
evidence.outcome: Deferral of cases to manual review via predefined safety criteria; accuracy of automated cases
evidence.effect: Colon-Pilot issued recommendations for 522 of 596 cases (87.6%) and flagged 12.4% for manual review. For automated cases, guideline-concordant accuracy was 97.5% (Cohen κ = 0.970) versus 69.7% for endoscopists.
evidence.quote: Colon-Pilot issued recommendations for 522 of 596 cases (87.6%) and flagged 12.4% for manual review.

evidence.title: Mechanistic interpretability of reinforcement learning in Medicaid care coordination
evidence.outcome: Whether conformal clearance separates low-harm decisions from those needing human review
evidence.effect: 89.5% of decisions cleared with 1.22% residual harm versus 6.67% harm among flagged decisions (81.7% relative reduction).
evidence.quote: Residual harm among cleared decisions was 1.22% (95% CI 1.14% to 1.30%) vs 6.67% (95% CI 6.02% to 7.32%) for flagged decisions, an 81.7% relative reduction ( table 2 ).

evidence.title: A confidence-based, artificial intelligence pathology model for diagnosis of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
evidence.venue: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
evidence.outcome: AUROC and false-positive rate with confidence thresholding
evidence.effect: AUROC improved to 0.958 with an FPR of 0, while retaining 46% of samples for high-confidence prediction
evidence.quote: Implementation of confidence thresholding improved the AUROC to 0.958 with an FPR of 0, while retaining 46% of samples for high-confidence prediction.
evidence.country: France, India, South Korea (with five European centers in retrospective set)

evidence.title: CALM-RAD: Calibrated GPT-4o Confidence-Based Triage Enables 96-100% Accuracy in Automated TNM Staging of Head and Neck Cancer Reports
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of GPT-4o TNM labels when uncertain cases are deferred via calibrated confidence triage
evidence.effect: Accepting 37% (simple) and 34% (structured) of T-stage predictions raised accuracies to 0.89 and 1.00; accepting 55% of N-stage cases achieved up to 1.00 accuracy.
evidence.quote: Triage thresholds accepting 37% (simple) and 34% (structured) of T-stage predictions raised accuracies to 0.89 and 1.00, respectively; accepting 55% of N-stage cases achieved up to 1.00 accuracy.

evidence.title: Adaptive AI for Cardiovascular Event Adjudication: Cardiovascular Event Adjudication Across Different Definitions in the ODYSSEY OUTCOMES and EUCLID Trials
evidence.outcome: F1 scores after routing low-certainty cases to humans
evidence.effect: Hybrid adjudication had highest F1: CV death 0.94, MI 0.80, stroke 0.82, bleeding 0.83.
evidence.quote: Hybrid adjudication F1 metrics were the highest (CV death, 0.94 [95% CI, 0.92-0.96]; MI, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.77-0.82]; stroke, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.78-0.86]; bleeding, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.82-0.85]).
evidence.sample_unit: suspected EUCLID primary end point events
evidence.country: International (ODYSSEY OUTCOMES and EUCLID multinational trials)

evidence.title: Correctness, Harmfulness, and Diversity of Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Comparative Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Deferral of incorrect responses to provider via automated filter, and cost of excessive deferral
evidence.effect: Filter cut error rates but did not penalize false deferrals; would likely be counterproductive if patients were redirected on answerable questions; harmful errors remained.
evidence.quote: If such a filter were deployed in patient interactions, it would likely be counterproductive: if patients are redirected to contact a provider for questions that could have been answered from the prep instructions, the usefulness of the AI Coach as an assistant for colonoscopy prep is undermined.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic dialogues per model (50 per model human-rated)

evidence.title: AT-CXR: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Triage for Chest X-rays
evidence.outcome: Selective-prediction performance (AURC, error at high coverage) of an agent that abstains on uncertain cases for human review
evidence.effect: Both AT-CXR routers achieved lower AURC and lower error at high coverage than zero-shot VLMs and supervised classifiers, with higher full-coverage accuracy. No numeric values in the text.
evidence.quote: Across five-fold evaluation on a balanced subset of NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset, both variants outperform strong zero-shot vision-language models and state-of-the-art supervised classifiers, achieving higher full-coverage accuracy and superior selective-prediction performance, evidenced by a lower area under the risk-coverage curve (AURC) and a lower error rate at high coverage, while operating with lower latency that meets practical clinical constraints.
evidence.sample_unit: chest X-ray images (balanced subset of NIH ChestX-ray14, five-fold)

evidence.title: KnowGuard: Knowledge-Driven Abstention for Multi-Round Clinical Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and number of interaction turns of abstention approaches in multi-round clinical benchmarks
evidence.effect: KnowGuard improved diagnostic accuracy by 3.93% and reduced unnecessary interaction by 7.27 turns on average versus state-of-the-art abstention approaches.
evidence.quote: Experimental evidences clearly demonstrate that KnowGuard outperforms state-of-the-art abstention approaches, improving diagnostic accuracy by 3.93\% while reducing unnecessary interaction by 7.27 turns on average.

evidence.title: Reliable Multilingual Orthopedic Decision Support from Clinical Narratives: Language-Aware Adaptation and Verification-Guided Deferral
evidence.outcome: Selective accuracy and Macro-F1 with deferral versus accept-all prediction
evidence.effect: Selective verification achieved 84.4% selective accuracy and 0.76 Macro-F1 at 72.3% coverage, versus 71.5% accuracy and 0.65 Macro-F1 for accept-all.
evidence.quote: On a randomly selected held-out 5,000-record subset, it achieves 84.4% selective accuracy and 0.76 selective Macro-F1 at 72.3% coverage, compared with 71.5% accuracy and 0.65 Macro-F1 for accept-all prediction.

evidence.title: Judge-dependent safety gains and model-specific helpfulness costs of evidence-sufficiency prompting in clinical LLMs
evidence.outcome: Unsafe overconfidence reduction and correct-diagnosis cost with evidence-sufficiency prompt that induces deferral/uncertainty
evidence.effect: Unsafe overconfidence fell from 49.3% to 24.7% (paired reduction 24.7 points, 95% CI 21.8-27.7); correct diagnosis fell from 80.3% to 50.3%; near-free for GPT-5.5, near-total for Gemini (-58 points).
evidence.quote: The gain carried a model-specific helpfulness cost (correct diagnosis 80.3% to 50.3%): near-free for GPT-5.5, near-total for Gemini (-58 points).
evidence.sample_unit: paired model-response cells (4 models x common panel of questions, standard vs wrapper prompt)

evidence.title: Knowing When Not to Decide: Multi-Pathology Chest X-Ray Classification with Rejection Mechanisms
evidence.outcome: Accuracy-coverage trade-off when model abstains on uncertain chest X-ray predictions and defers to experts
evidence.effect: Selective rejection improved the trade-off between diagnostic accuracy and coverage; entropy-based rejection gave the highest average AuC across all pathologies. No numeric values reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Experiments conducted on three large public datasets (PadChest, NIH ChestX-ray14, and MIMIC-CXR) demonstrate that selective rejection improves the trade-off between diagnostic accuracy and coverage, with entropy-based rejection yielding the highest average AuC across all pathologies.
evidence.sample_unit: chest X-ray images (three public datasets: PadChest, NIH ChestX-ray14, MIMIC-CXR)

evidence.title: Predictive Performance Precision Analysis in Medicine: Identification of low-confidence predictions at patient and profile levels (MED3pa I)
evidence.outcome: model sensitivity and AUC
evidence.effect: limiting predictions to the 93% most confident cases improved sensitivity by 14.3% and AUC by 5.1%
evidence.quote: In internal validation, limiting predictions to the 93% most confident cases improved sensitivity by 14.3% and the AUC by 5.1%.

evidence.title: Trustworthy LLM-Embedding Clinical Prediction: Calibrating Confidence and Transparency for Foundation Model-Based Disease Risk Scores
evidence.outcome: Clinician override rates
evidence.effect: 3.57% at moderate richness for 0.6B; 0% for larger models under default thresholds.
evidence.quote: The trust framework produced selective override rates contingent on both model capability and data richness (3.57% at moderate richness for the 0.6B model; 0% for larger models under default thresholds).

evidence.title: A Simulation-Based Validation Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Clinical Triage: Conformal Prediction and Ensemble Learning Applied to a Synthetic ICU Benchmark Cohort
evidence.outcome: Whether selective prediction/abstention improves performance on retained cases and isolates ambiguous cases
evidence.effect: Selective prediction raised AUC from 0.917 to 0.980 at 50% abstention; UNCERTAIN triage zone reached AUC 0.624 (chance level).
evidence.quote: Selective prediction raised AUC from 0.917 to 0.980 at 50% abstention.

evidence.title: Act or Defer: Error-Controlled Decision Policies for Medical Foundation Models
evidence.outcome: Whether calibrated deferral controls false discovery rate among acted-on cases and gives valid coverage for deferred patients
evidence.effect: StratCP controls the false discovery rate among selected patients and provides valid, selection-conditional coverage for deferred patients across ophthalmology and neuro-oncology tasks.
evidence.quote: Across tasks, S  trat CP controls the false discovery rate among selected patients and provides valid, selection-conditional coverage for deferred patients.

evidence.title: Development and retrospective validation of SCOUT: scalable clinical oversight of large language models via uncertainty triangulation
evidence.outcome: Whether LLM selectively defers unreliable predictions to clinicians without excessive review burden
evidence.effect: Deferral cut human review volume by 45% to 83% while projected accuracy reached 99.1% to 100.0% after expert correction of flagged cases.
evidence.quote: SCOUT reduced the volume of cases requiring human review by 45% to 83%, with projected final accuracy of 99.1% to 100.0% assuming expert correction of all flagged cases.

evidence.title: Calibrated Abstention and Clinical Deferral in Small Language Models via RLVR and GRPO
evidence.outcome: Abstention/deferral rate and accuracy before vs after RLVR/GRPO training on MedQA-USMLE
evidence.effect: Abstention rate rose from 3.5% to 8.0% (+129%), while raw accuracy fell from 44.0% to 35.5% (an 'Alignment Tax').
evidence.quote: Our results show a clear 'Alignment Tax' on raw accuracy (decreasing from 44.0% to 35.5% on MedQA-USMLE).

evidence.title: Condence, Calibration, and Abstention in Small Open-Weight Language Models on Psychiatric Knowledge Questions: A Cross-Domain Replication
evidence.outcome: Paired accuracy change when models were offered a prompted abstention option (deferral)
evidence.effect: Only the 1.2B model had a paired effect distinguishable from noise, and it was negative (-6.7 points, 95% CI [-12.7,-0.7]). The 7.6B model's effect reversed from a naive +0.8 to -5.3 points (95% CI [-9.3,-1.3]); 8 of 12 abstentions forfeited correct answers.
evidence.quote: a prompted abstention option is not a free safety improvement for any of the four models once evaluated with paired, coverage-aware statistics rather than naive answered-item accuracy.

evidence.title: Application of simultaneous uncertainty quantification for image segmentation with probabilistic deep learning: Performance benchmarking of oropharyngeal cancer target delineation as a use-case
evidence.outcome: Segmentation DSC improvement and fraction of patients referred when high-uncertainty cases were deferred
evidence.effect: Referring patients above uncertainty thresholds improved DSC by 4.7% (MC Dropout Ensemble) and 5.0% (Deep Ensemble) while referring 21.8% and 22% of patients.
evidence.quote: With referring patients based on uncertainty thresholds from 0.85 validation DSC for all uncertainty measures, on average the DSC improved from the full dataset by 4.7% and 5.0% while referring 21.8% and 22% patients for MC Dropout Ensemble and Deep Ensemble, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (PET/CT scans, external validation set; 224 for development)

evidence.title: Neonatal Pain Detection from Facial Expressions Using Deep Learning
evidence.outcome: Framework accuracy when low-confidence cases are deferred to manual assessment
evidence.effect: Overall framework accuracy reached 82.35% with the manual assessment branch integrated. The abstract says this integration raises recall of true pain events and reduces manual evaluation effort.
evidence.quote: Experimental results show our neural network sur- passes state-of-the-art algorithms by at least 25% in accuracy on the MNPAD dataset, with overall framework accuracy reaching 82.35% with integration of manual assessment branch.

evidence.title: Prompt Engineering Strategies Improve the Diagnostic Accuracy of GPT-4 Turbo in Neuroradiology Cases
evidence.outcome: Whether confidence-based deferral reduces misdiagnosis while limiting cases analyzed
evidence.effect: 90% confidence threshold reduced misdiagnoses from 29.4% to 14.1% and raised top-diagnosis accuracy to 72.9%, but restricted analysis to half of cases.
evidence.quote: Applying a 90% confidence threshold increased the accuracy of the top diagnosis to 72.9% and the applicability of the five candidates to 85.9%, while reducing misdiagnoses to 14.1%, but limited the analysis to half of cases.

evidence.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Classification of Adamantinomatous Craniopharyngioma from Preoperative MRI
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and abstention rate when model defers uncertain cases
evidence.effect: Abstention mechanism raised accuracy from 80.8% to 95.5% with a 34.2% (n=12) abstention rate; 10/12 abstained cases were NOTACP.
evidence.quote: Specifically, we observed an accuracy of 95.5%, sensitivity of 0.933, specificity of 0.833, FNR of 0.067, and FPR of 0.125.

evidence.title: InsightSleepNet: the interpretable and uncertainty-aware deep learning network for sleep staging using continuous Photoplethysmography
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Sleep staging accuracy, kappa and weighted F1 before versus after applying energy-score uncertainty threshold for selective prediction
evidence.effect: MESA accuracy rose from 84.2% to 84.8-86.1%; CFS from 80.6% to 81.9-85.6%; CAP from 80.6% to 81.4-84.3%. Kappa and weighted F1 also improved.
evidence.quote: We observed a significant improvement in the model's performance with the implementation of the energy score threshold.

evidence.title: U-PASS: An uncertainty-guided deep learning pipeline for automated sleep staging
evidence.outcome: sleep staging accuracy after deferral
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved from 75% to 85%; largest improvement gain due to deferral of uncertain epochs to a sleep expert.
evidence.quote: By optimizing the training dataset, actively seeking feedback from domain experts for informative samples, and deferring the most uncertain samples to experts, U-PASS achieves an impressive expert-level accuracy of 85% on a challenging clinical dataset of elderly sleep apnea patients.

evidence.title: Development and Validation of an Interpretable Conformal Predictor to Predict Sepsis Mortality Risk: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: Complex cases flagged for clinician review
evidence.effect: Flagged survivors had more AKI (22.4% vs 20.2%; 24% vs 20.4%) and longer ICU stays (89 vs 55; 78 vs 55 hours).
evidence.quote: In addition, for those patients who survived, the analysis showed that patients identified for clinician review (those with uncertain predictions) were more likely to develop new acute kidney injury after the first day of ICU admission (n=227, 22.4% vs n=428, 20.2% for MIMIC-IV; n=799, 24% vs n=875, 20.4% for eICU-CRD) and had longer ICU stays with a median of 89 (IQR 54-173) hours versus 55 (IQR 37-99) hours for MIMIC-IV, and 78 (IQR 48-141) hours versus 55 (IQR 40-91) hours for eICU-CRD, compared to the patients who were not flagged for review.

evidence.title: Optimizing GPT-4 Turbo Diagnostic Accuracy in Neuroradiology through Prompt Engineering and Confidence Thresholds
evidence.outcome: Trade-off between confidence-threshold deferral and number of cases answered
evidence.effect: The 90% confidence threshold improved precision but reduced the number of cases that received a response (no numbers given in abstract).
evidence.quote: However, this threshold reduced the number of cases that responded.

evidence.title: Large-scale deep learning for metastasis detection in pathology reports
evidence.outcome: Recall when model defers uncertain reports to human review
evidence.effect: Retaining 72.9% of reports (deferring the rest to humans) increased recall from 0.894 to 0.969.
evidence.quote: We found that retaining 72.9% of reports increased recall from 0.894 to 0.969.

evidence.title: Quantifying Epistemic Uncertainty in Predictions for Safer Health AI Performance Under Dataset Shifts
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: macro-F1 and prediction error capture under temporal drift
evidence.effect: samples below 95% uncertainty threshold had consistently higher macro-F1 and performance invariant to temporal drift, while flagged samples captured most errors
evidence.quote: Results across all training-test time pairs show that samples below this threshold exhibit consistently higher macro-F1 and render performance virtually invariant to temporal drift, while the flagged samples captured most prediction errors.

evidence.title: Automated real-time assessment of intracranial hemorrhage detection AI using an ensembled monitoring model (EMM)
evidence.outcome: Low-confidence deferral accuracy and false alarms
evidence.effect: ICH-positive: +4.66, +11.28, and +38.57% versus false alarms 0.89, 0.45, and 0.14%; ICH-negative net benefit only at 30%.
evidence.quote: However, this net benefit was only observed for cases with ICH-negative primary model predictions at 30% prevalence (false-alarm rate of 1.05% versus relative accuracy improvement of 3.35%).

evidence.title: Semantic Consistency-Based Uncertainty Quantification for Factuality in Radiology Report Generation
evidence.outcome: Factuality score gain from abstaining on high-uncertainty generated radiology reports
evidence.effect: Abstaining from high-uncertainty reports improved factuality scores by 10%, achieved by rejecting 20% of reports (Radialog, MIMIC-CXR).
evidence.quote: By abstaining from high-uncertainty reports, our approach improves factuality scores by 10%, achieved by rejecting 20% of reports using the Radialog model on the MIMIC-CXR dataset.

evidence.title: PEER: Towards reliable and efficient inference via Patience-Based Early Exiting with Rejection
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and abstention rate when uncertain samples are rejected for human review versus baseline
evidence.effect: On MIMIC-III, PEER reached 90.73% accuracy versus 89.48% baseline by rejecting only 2.79% of uncertain samples.
evidence.quote: For instance, on the MIMIC-III dataset, PEER achieves an accuracy of 90.73% (surpassing the baseline of 89.48%) by rejecting only 2.79% of uncertain samples.

evidence.title: Hallucination filtering in radiology vision-language models using discrete semantic entropy
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of VLM answers after deferring/excluding high-semantic-entropy questions
evidence.effect: Filtering DSE > 0.3 raised accuracy from 51.7% to 76.3% for GPT-4o (334/706 retained) and 54.8% to 63.8% for GPT-4.1 (499/706 retained), both p < 0.001.
evidence.quote: After filtering out high-entropy questions (DSE > 0.3), accuracy on the remaining questions was 76.3% (retained questions: 334/706) for GPT-4o and 63.8% (retained questions: 499/706) for GPT-4.1 (both p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Question Answering on a Heart Failure Dataset: Performance Analysis
evidence.outcome: LLM classifier accuracy in identifying answerable, deferral, and nonanswerable heart failure queries
evidence.effect: Classifier achieved 65% accuracy for answerable and helpful deferral queries and 100% accuracy for identifying nonanswerable queries.
evidence.quote: The pipeline first uses an LLM-based classifier, achieving 65% accuracy for answerable and helpful deferral queries and 100% accuracy for identifying nonanswerable queries.

evidence.title: AI-Based Dementia Prediction From Low-Dose Brain CT in Mild Cognitive Impairments

commentary.bottom_line: Studies suggest that confidence-based deferral may raise accuracy on the cases an AI tool keeps while reducing human review burden. Nearly all tests are offline replays, and few measure how often high-risk cases are missed or answerable questions are needlessly deferred.

perspectives.view: Three studies tested the practice in real deployment: one randomized trial, one prospective comparison, and one quasi-experimental study. The remaining studies were offline replays, simulations, or benchmarks. The trial reported a 65% drop in standard-risk queries routed to humans but did not quantify missed high-risk deferrals. Results point one way, but indirectness and sparse over-deferral data support low certainty.

In replays, deferral raised accuracy from 0.847 for AI alone to 0.869, and cleared decisions carried 1.22% harm versus 6.67% among flagged ones. Hazard benchmarks show models selecting an answer in 53-82% of items lacking a correct option. This suggests a tool's deferral behavior should be tested before use rather than assumed.

Consistency-based deferral raised F1 to 0.62-0.73 on a harder step, but the gains were marginal because confidence was poorly calibrated. In one benchmark, safety-aware prompting reduced premature commitment only by shifting errors toward excessive abstention. These results suggest deferral thresholds may need local tuning and ongoing monitoring of both under-deferral and over-deferral.

Replays reported 66% less clinician workload in breast screening, a 68.9% workload reduction in pathology, and a 75% cut in manual review. One Vietnamese study found that sending every clinically significant disagreement for a second read would raise burden by 6.67%. These figures suggest staffing effects depend on where the deferral threshold is set.

One simulation found that an automated filter reduced errors but did not penalize false deferrals. Its authors judged it likely counterproductive if patients were redirected on answerable questions, and harmful errors remained. In another study, models flagged text-assessable items as not assessable more often than clinicians did (19.4% vs. 11.4%).

One replay used 250,000 Medicaid intervention records, and one used Finnish-language patient records. Both were offline analyses, and no test reported low-literacy populations. Hazard studies in Turkish and Italian found concordance on specialist-referral coding as low as 37.5% and a model answering when it should not.

A regulatory discussion paper describes checking whether a device defers when information is insufficient without over-deferring when information is adequate. One prospective offline study reported 12.4% of colonoscopy cases flagged for manual review and 97.5% accuracy on automated cases. Few tests report a rate of unnecessary deferral of the kind the paper describes.

commentary.research_gap: No study measures, in live clinical use, both the rate of missed deferrals on high-risk or complex cases and the rate of unnecessary deferrals on answerable questions. No study links deferral behavior to patient outcomes and clinician workload. Prospective deployment studies that report these paired measures are lacking, as are live studies in Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, and low-literacy settings.
commentary.underserved_note: Two tests included underserved or language-diverse populations: one offline replay of Medicaid decision records (pmid:41667212) and one offline replay of Finnish-language records (epmc:PPR1276359). No test reported low-literacy populations, and none of the real-deployment studies reported underserved populations. Evidence for these groups therefore rests on retrospective data and may not reflect how deferral performs in live care for them.
